title: I'm Not Running by David Hare with Sian Brooke - review
transcript: I'm not running by David Hare directed by Neil and field and starring Sean Brooke at the National Theatre London a new play by one of our greatest living playwrights David Hare and starting a fine actor like Sean Brooks sounded like a safe bet so you can imagine my disappointment when I was confronted by a contrived plot weighted conflict and a predictable end and an acting performance that offered none of the charisma that the role seemed to suggest to be fair - oh and Brooke maybe the script rather than that was lacking rather than her performance the plot concerns a clash between a doctor who's run a single-issue political campaign to save the local hospital and subsequently becomes an MP and a career politician with whom she has chose a history and by the way Alex hassel has a sparring partner gives a bravura performance and ranges from tears to tantrums the play jumps back and forth between the present day and the events that led up to it we see the main character developing a political understanding to the point where she's considering running or not running for the Labor Party leadership David hare tries to help our political understanding - so we see how the personal political eclectic connected how we need political parties in this case the Labour Party if we want to change things but also how Westminster we need Leicester in the party line was putting efficiency before people less male ego and more passion more belief more women the play takes its time and if you're not interested in politics you may find it dull although there are some juicy confrontations the problem for me is that the arguments were also one-sided so the excitement never mounts and far from be carried along to the climax I had plenty of time to consider how unlikely it was another thing this intimate plane prize is almost entirely of conversations between two people in small rooms the large auditorium leads to performances that are really more shouty than they should be I give I'm not running three stars found this review useful and you don't want to miss the next one please subscribe to one minute theater reviews by clicking on the icon at the bottom of the screen you
